title: Peder Vibe to Peder Juel, Danish resident in Stockholm, 1649-1651, cipher passages in the old cipher ("gamle Ciffres") of 10 letters or pages (part of catalogue 2527, Rigsarkivet TKUA Sverige): cyclic shift-per-word alphabet recovered, nomenclator open: read in part

steps.what: Cipher passages of images 62-74 transcribed number by number by the contributor's agents; image 74 hashed in the held-out set of test 1 before any decryption; all re-read at native zoom afterwards.
The shift-per-word system (opener + body, body = rank + k) found on N. 319 (image 78), a letter in the new alphabet of the same unit, from its interlinear letters of the time.

Test 1 (pre-registered; protocol hashed before the set was opened, by the contributor's record): one opener table for the whole unit, that of N. 319, 23-letter alphabet; held-out images 74 (N. 330), 77 (N. 316), 79 right (N. 334), 54 words, 335 numbers. M1 -3.068 against a best of 600 controls of -3.281: margin 0.21, under the bar of 0.30. FAILED; not measured again. Cause found afterwards: N. 330 is in the old cipher.

After test 1: N. 330 (image 74) read with a cyclic 23-letter alphabet and k = -(opener mod 3), and tied to Vibe's clear remark on image 62 that he is writing in the old cipher. The rule was found on a set already measured and opened, and was never put to a pre-registered test.
The ten letters or pages of 1649-1651 read with the fixed rule: 250 cipher words (the contributor: 212 certain, 31 probable, 1 restored, 6 unresolved); 68 nomenclator codes not identified.

Independent verification of PR #410 before integration: test 1 re-run with identical figures (failed); frozen hashes match; a second decoder gives the same decryption; image 74 (about 110 numbers) and image 62 agree with the transcription. Later controls, after the fact: image 74 alone with the frozen table of test 1 scores -3.980 against a best control of -3.125; the fixed old-cipher rule scores -1.926 against a best of -2.536 for 200 random opener tables; a per-letter refit of k agrees with the fixed tables for 383 of 403 words of both ciphers.

Integration: target split by key out of vibejuel1651 (old cipher here, new alphabet there, Krag letters to a lead); eval() replaced by ast.literal_eval in scripts/decode.py with byte-identical output; counts taken again (250 words, 68 codes, as in the PR); last cipher word of image 62 re-divided on the image as 27.12.1.11.3.14.13.19.1.13.19 = malcontant (probable), so 244 of 250 words have a value; outcome.key set to partial, fraction_read 0.976, codes_open 68, read_share 0.667; reading read as sentences against the translation (grade B).

Register p. 115 (Juel to Vibe, 2 Sep 1648; PR #457) added from juel1647: the rule applied unchanged reads 21 certain words of 25 (23 in the contributor's count), 15 code tokens open; an own decoder reproduces the decryption; image 61 compared at integration, no disagreement; three nomenclator numbers (212, 351, 401) also occur in the letters of 1649-51. Not a pre-registered test; counted apart from the headline of the ten letters.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: No letter in this cipher has a gloss. The shift-per-word system was found from the partial interlinear decipherment of the time on N. 319 (image 78, new alphabet) in the same unit; the old cipher's cyclic 23-letter alphabet and opener rule were then worked out on N. 330 and the letters of 1649-50, and the cipher is named in Vibe's clear text on image 62. The nomenclator is not recovered.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading.md: 244 of 250 cipher words in letters given a value (212 certain + 32 probable; 1 restored and 5 unresolved are holes) = 97.6%. The 68 nomenclator code tokens are counted apart (codes_open); with them as holes the read share is 244/318 = 76.7% (texts[].read_share).

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out tests (not docs/_validate.py). The old-cipher rule has no pre-registered test. Test 1, the only one whose held-out set included a letter in this cipher (N. 330, image 74), FAILED: one opener table for the whole unit, M1 -3.068 against a best control of -3.281, margin 0.21 under the bar of 0.30; N. 330 is not in that table. Test 2 (rule changed after test 1) passed on new-alphabet letters only and does not cover this cipher. Later controls made at verification, after the fact: the fixed rule scores -1.926 against a best of -2.536 for 200 random opener tables; image 74 reads frychter, at directly.

texts.label: Peder Vibe to Peder Juel, 1649-1651, cipher passages in the old cipher of 10 letters or pages
texts.summary: News of the Danish court from Copenhagen, January 1649 to September 1651: who obtains what from #211 and who is reconciled with whom; sailors and every man discontented while the Marselis and Friedrich Möller hold assignments on the best revenues of the realm; the High Steward kept at home by a pretended weakness; #228 asking satisfaction for an arrest and #211 a declaration about an alleged murder plot; the account of the Norwegian fleet; #422 to be judged; how to win #370 away from #422. The 22 code numbers that name the actors are not identified.

reading_review.by: Brice Dudout's AI agents; re-read at integration by an AI agent for the project
reading_review.note: Contributor: read as Danish sentences by AI agents only; no human read it. Integration (PR #410): reading.md read letter by letter against decryption.txt and translation.md; the cipher words construe with the clear words around them and the translation follows; but 68 code tokens stand for the persons and places, so who does what is mostly open, 32 words are only probable and 5 unresolved: grade B, read in part. Image 62 and part of image 74 were compared with the images.

texts.label: p. 115 of Juel's register, to Peder Vibe, 2 Sep 1648
texts.summary: 442 said some days ago to 212 that the former 412 of 351 277 [...] her away, and that 401 shall now bring her back here again; the 412 of 426 drove with three wagons between. The codes name the people; none is identified.
texts.note: 25 cipher words: 21 certain verbatim (84.0%; two more, bort and skal, rest on digits settled by the blind review and count as probable here), 1 guess, 1 hole; 15 code tokens (nine numbers, 212, 351 and 401 also in the letters of 1649-51) counted as holes: 21 of 40 = 52.5%. The contributor counted 23 of 25 (92.0%). The clear text of the register between the runs is not transcribed.

reading_review.note: The cipher words read almost fully as Danish and the sense of the first sentence is clear: 442 said that the former 412 of 351 277 [...] her away and that 401 shall now bring her back. The holes are codes and untranscribed clear text, not failed decryption; the reviewer asked for that clear text to be transcribed.

outcome.notes: Split out of vibejuel1651 on 12 Nov 2026 (one key, one entry): the new alphabet of 1651-1655 is targets/vibejuel1651, with the frozen test files of both tests. The key (key.tsv, CC BY 4.0) was applied to p. 115 of Juel's register (catalogue 2553). Prior art was not searched again at verification or integration. Register p. 115 (Juel to Vibe, 2 Sep 1648) added 12 Nov 2026 from PR #457; the headline figures are those of the ten letters of 1649-51 and p. 115 is counted apart.

prior.where: No decipherment of the old-cipher letters is known. The only decipherment of the time in the unit is the partial gloss on N. 319 (image 78), a letter in the new alphabet. Catalogue 2527 vetting (Daniel Bourdeau, 11 Nov 2026): DECODE, Tomokiyo, Lasry nothing. Fryxell 1836 gives a Swedish abstract of Juel's register without the cipher passages. The contributor's web search of 11 Nov 2026 found no edition. Not searched again at verification or integration.

human: Brice Dudout chose the target and set the rules (protocol hashed before each single measurement; a partial reading may be published if explained). His AI agents transcribed, found the system, wrote and ran the protocols, read and wrote up. No human read the reading. At integration (12 Nov 2026) the project re-ran the scripts, split the target by key and recounted.
